lines.trans: Mr. Muranishi, we have to set up a proper shipping plan.
Sales are through the roof—let's keep pushing them out!
I admit they are selling, yet I am the one who decides how we sell them.

words.gram: Conjunction trailing off to soften hesitation.

lines.trans: Besides, we must think about the company's long-term direction.
Rivals are already copying us. We have to stay one step ahead.
There is zero planning! We are short-handed—the crew will collapse!
Business is booming! A resort villa just hit the market—why not buy it?
I will buy it, once the satellite deal goes through.
I am deeply sorry. I will have a firm talk with Muranishi.
Could you somehow let him appear on the program again?
It really is a golden opportunity.
Yes, of course. Thank you very much.

lines.trans: See you.

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Reassures that rules or steps are followed properly.

examples.text: ちゃんと確認しました。
ちゃんと並んでいます。
村西さん、ちゃんと出荷計画立てないと。
examples.trans: Mr. Muranishi, we have to set up a proper shipping plan.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 売り上げ好調ですよ、どんどんいきましょう！
examples.trans: Sales are through the roof—let's keep pushing them out!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.note: Acknowledges that what the other person pointed out really is true.

examples.text: 確かにそのとおりですね。
確かに受け取りました。

meanings.note: Intransitive verb describing goods selling on the market without naming a seller.

examples.text: この絵本はよく売れます。
新しい本がたくさん売れました。
examples.trans: Many copies of the new book sold.

meanings.note: Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.
Connects a contrasting fact or trails off at the end of a sentence to voice a polite objection.

examples.text: お風呂に入りましたけど。
examples.trans: I already took a bath, though.

examples.text: 高いけど、おいしいです。

meanings.note: Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: て-form 売って links 'sell' into the next action.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Ichidan verb; potential form 決められる means 'can decide'.

examples.text: まだ何も決めていません。
今決められないなら、後で考えましょう。
examples.trans: If you can't decide now, let's think about it later.

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
In casual speech, それ plus は often fuses into そりゃ ('well, as for that / of course').

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Everyday word for a business company or one's workplace.

examples.text: 新しい会社に入りました。

examples.trans: The company is near the station.

examples.text: 一斉摘発をする方針を発表いたしました。
examples.trans: Authorities announced a policy of simultaneous nationwide raids.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb.

examples.text: もう少しよく考えてみます。
examples.trans: I'll think about it a little more carefully.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

examples.text: 無計画すぎるんですよ。人も足りてないし、倒れちゃいますよ？
examples.trans: There is zero planning! We are short-handed—the crew will collapse!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Read ひと when standing as an independent noun.

examples.text: 親切な人に会いました。
無計画すぎるんですよ。人も足りてないし、倒れちゃいますよ？
examples.trans: There is zero planning! We are short-handed—the crew will collapse!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 絶好調ですね。今ちょうど別荘が売りに出てるんです。買っちゃいません？
examples.trans: Business is booming! A resort villa just hit the market—why not buy it?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').

examples.text: 前に薦めてきた別荘、クルーザー、土地はいくらだ？
examples.trans: How much are that villa, cruiser, and land you pitched me earlier?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: 買えます is the polite potential form meaning 'can buy / can afford to buy'.

examples.text: 本屋で雑誌を買いました。
examples.trans: I bought a magazine at the bookstore.

examples.text: この値段なら買えますよ。
examples.trans: At this price, we can buy it.

examples.text: そんなことしたら世の中がめちゃくちゃになりますよ！
examples.trans: If you aired things like that on television, society would fall apart!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.

examples.text: そうです。この巨大アンテナから飛んだ電波を衛星がキャッチするんです。
examples.trans: That's right. Orbiting satellites catch the waves beamed from these giant antennas.

examples.text: そして今度は衛星から地球に電波が降り注ぐ。
examples.trans: And then the signals shower back down from the satellite onto the earth.

examples.text: もちろん。そのための衛星だ。
examples.trans: Of course. That is what the satellite is for.

meanings.note: I-adjective; adverbial form うまく means 'well' or 'smoothly' (as in うまくいく).

examples.text: 計画がうまくいきました。
彼は英語がとてもうまいです。
examples.trans: He is very good at English.

examples.text: 誠に申し訳ございません。村西には言って聞かせますんで。
examples.trans: I am deeply sorry. I will have a firm talk with Muranishi.

examples.text: 本日は私どものためにお集まりいただき誠にありがとうございます！
examples.trans: Thank you all so much for gathering out here for us today!

meanings.en: justification (申し訳ございません = no excuse / deeply sorry)
meanings.note: Paired with ございません or ありません for formal apologies.

examples.text: 遅れて申し訳ございません。
examples.trans: I am deeply sorry for being late.

examples.text: 大変申し訳ありませんでした。

meanings.en: polite auxiliary in ありがとうございます
meanings.note: Survives in modern speech chiefly in ございます (present) and ございました (past) after ありがとう and おめでとう.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。
ありがとうございました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much (for what just concluded).

examples.text: 皆さんの意見をお聞かせください。
examples.trans: Please let me hear your opinions.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: side or option in comparisons and advice (〜ほうがいい)
meanings.note: Paired with がいい after past or negative forms to recommend the better course ('it is better to...').

examples.text: 早く寝たほうがいいよ。
examples.trans: You had better go to sleep early.

examples.text: 傘を持ったほうがいいです。
examples.trans: It is better to bring an umbrella.

examples.text: 出演のほうはなんとか再開してもらえませんか？
examples.trans: Could you somehow let him appear on the program again?

examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: よかったら来てください。
ええ、また機会を設けてじっくり話したいようです。
examples.trans: Yes, he wants to set up a proper occasion to talk with you at length.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Confident everyday word that works either before a predicate or as a standalone answer.

examples.text: もちろん手伝いますよ。

meanings.note: Standalone casual thanks; followed by ございます (present) or ございました (completed occasion) for polite thanks.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。

meanings.note: Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.
